concepts: Parallel token release / tokens per forward
Certainty forcing to a release threshold
contributions: Quantifies the state-action mismatch in off-policy few-step dLLM distillation: only 33.7% of student-visited states lie on the teacher trajectory (6.5% after step 40), and only 50.3% of verifier-approved merges stay outcome-preserving when transferred from a progress-matched teacher state to the student state.

Consistency-guided adaptive compression: a state-dependent rule that orders outcome-aligned future candidates by teacher confidence and selects the longest prefix whose joint commitment leaves the frozen teacher's rollout outcome unchanged, with a lemma establishing that the selection is well defined and costs at most |C(x)| counterfactual checks.

Evidence that joint rather than token-wise verification is the right unit: 10 of 416 unions of individually valid tokens fail the joint check, and joint testing buys accuracy where independent testing buys speed.

A verified-set transition objective combining a max-hinge set bottleneck that promotes the least-ready verified token to the release threshold with a frozen-teacher KL anchor on all other active positions, and an argument for keeping the teacher frozen (refreshing it collapses the anchor KL to 4.66e-9 and leaves only recursive confidence sharpening).

A quality-efficiency evaluation across four math and code benchmarks reporting the highest average quality-constrained AUP (313.18) among the evaluated few-step baselines, with the accuracy cost stated openly.

A compression-space audit showing how much merge depth is actually available on student states (mean verified horizon 2.41 waves, realised span capped at 3.16x, empty candidate set in 31.4% of states).
limitations: Stated: the outcome-consistency guarantee covers target construction under the frozen teacher and verifier, neither of which exists at inference -- the student releases whatever its learned confidences pass, so inference-time quality is an empirical property of calibration, not a guaranteed one. Confidence calibration and cross-backbone transfer are left open. The complete-stack table mixes different native decoders and must not be read as isolating transition distillation. The state-source and fixed-vs-adaptive curves are single-seed. The base-LLaDA transfer changes several training and decoding factors at once, so it is evidence of transfer rather than a controlled initializer ablation. The set-bottleneck loss is not claimed to dominate at every operating point (it is behind mean hinge at 256 updates), and at nearest-speed operating points the paired difference is not significant (p = 0.930). Worth noticing beyond those: the primary operating point loses 3.41 accuracy points to the initialiser it was distilled from, so the practical claim rests on AUP -- an area measure with a chosen alpha = 3 weighting and a five-accuracy-point endpoint filter, both of which shape the ranking; the decoder-matched gain is only +0.67 accuracy and +4.4% TPF, which is the honest size of the learned-policy effect; there is no NFE reduction at all, so wall-clock benefit depends on how the extra tokens per forward interact with cache and batching, which is not measured here; and the compression audit shows the method's own ceiling is about 3.2x realised span with an empty candidate set in 31.4% of states, so the mechanism is inactive for roughly a third of decoding states.
method: The student is run from a fully masked response with the same question-only dynamic decoder used at inference, to a sampled depth, giving an on-policy root state x and the exposed block group. A frozen, question-only teacher (it sees only the question and x, never a gold answer) completes that block group conservatively through a sequence of release waves, yielding a rollout outcome x_T, with the wave horizon capped at 16. A candidate set C(x) keeps masked positions whose current teacher argmax already equals their value in the rollout outcome, ordered by decreasing teacher confidence with position as tie-breaker. The compression extent is then chosen by a joint test rather than a token-wise one: scanning prefixes from longest to shortest, OPTD takes the largest m such that committing the first wave plus the first m candidates all at once leaves the teacher's rollout outcome unchanged. Lemma 1 notes the empty prefix is always consistent -- it is the ordinary first teacher transition -- so the selection is well defined and the returned action is jointly outcome-preserving, at a cost of at most |C(x)| counterfactual outcome checks; the guarantee is prefix-relative, not optimal over arbitrary subsets. Training then has two terms. A set-bottleneck certainty loss takes the max over the verified set of the hinge [log tau - log p_theta(y_i)]_+, so it is zero only once every verified candidate has reached the decoder's release threshold and otherwise pushes the least-ready member. A frozen-teacher KL anchor holds all other active positions, including the already-releasable first wave, at the teacher's current-state distribution. The teacher stays frozen deliberately: refreshing it to the current student collapses the anchor KL and leaves only self-reinforcing confidence sharpening. No gold response, auxiliary head or inference-time verifier is involved; at inference the unchanged student and decoder run alone.
methods: consistency-guided adaptive compression / joint outcome verification
baselines: LLaDA, Fast-dLLM, D2F, dParallel, d3LLM, TAD-Q, TAD-S
one_liner: OPTD trains a few-step diffusion language model by sampling partial decoding states from the student's own inference trajectory and letting a frozen teacher verify, per state, the longest set of future token releases that can be committed jointly without changing the teacher's rollout outcome.
problem: Masked diffusion language models decode by repeatedly filling masked positions, and a threshold decoder can commit several confident tokens per forward pass, but accurate generation still needs many neural function evaluations. Few-step distillation compresses several teacher denoising transitions into one student transition; existing methods build that supervision off-policy, on fixed teacher trajectories or prescribed corruption schedules. Because one parallel commitment changes the context of every remaining mask, the states the accelerated student actually visits drift away from the supervised ones, and the drift is worst exactly where compression is most aggressive. On-policy collection fixes the state mismatch but leaves open how far a single transition should advance: matching only the teacher's next action gives no compression, a fixed merge horizon applies the same depth everywhere, and verifying candidate tokens one at a time misses the fact that tokens valid in isolation can be invalid when committed together.

relevance.overthinking: Tangential. The topic matched on the phrase 'adaptive compression', but what is being compressed here is the number of denoising steps a masked diffusion language model takes to fill in a fixed 256-token response -- not the length of a reasoning trace, and not any decision about how long a model should think. The paper's 'transitions' are decoder update steps, its 'compression' is how many masked positions can be committed in one forward pass, and its adaptivity is per decoding state, not per problem difficulty. It never measures reasoning length, never varies the thinking budget, and its efficiency metric (tokens per forward) explicitly does not correspond to fewer generated tokens: average NFE is unchanged (34.74 vs 34.87) and OPTD's outputs are in fact 2.62% longer than the baseline's. The only contact with the topic is incidental: it evaluates on GSM8K and MATH-500, and it reports an accuracy/efficiency trade-off curve of the same shape the topic cares about (+38.1% throughput for -3.41 accuracy points against its own initialiser). If anything from it is reusable, it is the methodological point that individually valid decisions can be jointly invalid, and the finding that supervision collected off the student's own trajectory covers only 33.7% of the states it visits -- both are general on-policy-distillation observations rather than results about reasoning length.

results: Student and frozen teacher are initialised from the released TAD-Speed checkpoint over LLaDA-8B-Instruct; rank-128 LoRA, learning rate 1e-6; confidence Multi-Block decoding with 256-token responses, 32-token blocks, at most 3 active blocks, threshold 0.8. Evaluation is GSM8K (5-shot), MATH-500 (4-shot), MBPP (3-shot, all 500 problems), HumanEval (0-shot), BF16 greedy, reporting accuracy or pass@1, NFE, tokens per forward (TPF) and a quality-constrained AUP. Complete-stack comparison with each method's native decoder: OPTD averages 47.21 accuracy at 7.87 TPF and 313.18 AUP, against TAD-S 50.62 / 5.70 / 245.59, TAD-Q 51.90 / 5.13 / 218.07, d3LLM 45.38 / 6.94 / 230.50, dParallel 45.84 / 5.04 / 156.48, Fast-dLLM 47.88 / 2.54 / 107.84 and vanilla LLaDA 46.82 / 1.00 / 46.82. So the headline is 27.5% higher AUP than the best prior method and 6.69x vanilla, obtained as +38.1% TPF against TAD-S in exchange for 3.41 accuracy points -- the paper states plainly that this is a high-parallelism operating point, not a uniformly accuracy-preserving method. Under a matched decoder the residual effect of the learned policy is much smaller: macro accuracy 47.30 to 47.97 (+0.67) and TPF 6.86 to 7.16 (+4.4%). Against d3LLM on full GSM8K with one evaluator and a single-block prefix-cache decoder, accuracy rises 75.13 to 79.91 and TPF 6.842 to 6.995, correcting 157 examples and regressing 94 (exact McNemar p = 8.41e-5); average NFE is essentially unchanged (34.74 vs 34.87) and outputs are 2.62% longer, and the authors explicitly do not claim an NFE reduction -- the TPF gain is more tokens per forward, not fewer forwards. The state-mismatch audit that motivates the method: only 33.7% of student-visited states appear on the corresponding teacher trajectory (95% Wilson CI [30.9, 36.6]), falling from 55.0% in decoding steps 0-7 to 6.5% after step 40, while normalised Hamming distance to the nearest teacher state rises from 0.0119 to 0.4510; and of verifier-approved merges on progress-matched teacher states, only 50.3% remain outcome-preserving after transfer to the student state (78.9% early, 14.3% after step 40). Ablations: on-policy vs off-policy state source at matched everything else gives macro accuracy 47.14 / 47.85 / 48.51 at 256 / 512 / 1,024 updates, with the gap over off-policy going from -0.20 to +0.78 to +1.88 points at nearly identical TPF (7.217 vs 7.233) -- single seed, so a learning curve rather than a variance estimate. Set-bottleneck loss beats mean hinge 47.62 vs 46.04 accuracy at similar TPF and projection KL 46.20. Joint verification admits fewer tokens per state than independent verification (1.327 vs 2.875) but 10 of 416 unions of individually valid tokens fail the joint check; joint testing gains 0.67 / 0.89 accuracy points at 256 / 512 updates while independent testing gains 0.16 / 0.26 TPF. Refreshing the teacher gives 79.98 / 6.285 against 81.05 / 6.171 frozen, with anchor KL collapsing from 0.00697 to 4.66e-9. The available compression is limited: at threshold 0.9 the mean first wave is 9.43 tokens, the verified set 4.52, the merged action 13.94, mean verified horizon 2.41 waves, and the candidate set is empty in 31.4% of states; a requested 8x span is fully available in only 10.1% of states and the realised span caps at 3.16x (3.17x with rank-256 LoRA), with utilisation 21.2% at a requested 16x. Adaptive versus fixed horizon, verification disabled in both arms and starting from base LLaDA: at H=2 accuracy is unchanged (+0.08) for +7.2% TPF, while H=4 and H=8 trade 1.05-1.53 accuracy points for 20.7-29.2% more TPF, and fixed-horizon TPF actually falls from 4.824 to 4.116 as H grows. Training from base LLaDA-8B-Instruct without the TAD-S initialiser reaches 47.96 macro accuracy at 3.78 TPF and 138.77 AUP, less than half the primary TPF, which the authors attribute mainly to the initialiser supplying cross-block parallelism without claiming causation, since the recipes are not matched. All results are GPU inference; no hardware or human evaluation.
